analysis.investment_thesis: Jayaswal Neco fails the Magic Formula on both dimensions: earnings yield of ~5.5% (EBIT ₹657 Cr / EV ~₹11,942 Cr) is below the 6% threshold, and ROCE of 2.93% is far below the 20% minimum for a quality business. At a P/E of 25x on rapidly collapsing earnings (₹2,247 Cr → ₹113 Cr over three years), the market is pricing in a recovery that the numbers do not support.
key_strengths: OCF consistently positive (5/5 years), with FCF surging to ₹1,144 Cr in FY25 — debt repayment is real
Debt declining steadily: ₹3,845 Cr (FY22) → ₹2,753 Cr (FY25), trajectory is correct
Diversified product mix (steel, castings, pipes) serving auto, railways, infrastructure reduces single-customer risk
key_risks: Finance cost (₹554 Cr) consumes 84% of EBIT (₹657 Cr) — almost no earnings reach equity holders
Net profit in freefall: ₹2,247 Cr (FY22, one-time) → ₹227 → ₹210 → ₹113 Cr; underlying business earns very little
Commodity steel has no pricing power or moat; revenue flat at ~₹6,000 Cr for four years with margins compressing
red_flags: FY22 net profit of ₹2,247 Cr was almost certainly a one-time debt-restructuring gain, not operating performance — current P/E of 25x is based on ₹113 Cr normalized earnings, implying true P/E is far higher
ROCE of 2.93% and ROE of -0.87% — capital is being destroyed, not compounded
EBITDA shrinking: ₹1,333 Cr (FY22) → ₹947 Cr (FY25), yet interest expense is rising to ₹554 Cr — interest coverage is razor-thin at ~1.7x
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Jayaswal Neco is a textbook Magic Formula reject. Earnings yield (EBIT/EV) is roughly 5.5% — below the 6% floor that signals cheapness — and ROCE of 2.93% is catastrophically below the 20% threshold that separates good businesses from capital destroyers. The business earned ₹657 Cr in EBIT in FY25 against ₹554 Cr in finance costs, meaning debt servicing alone absorbs over 84% of operating earnings. What reaches net income (₹113 Cr on a ₹9,345 Cr market cap) is a rounding error. The much-touted FY22 profit of ₹2,247 Cr was a non-recurring event — likely a debt haircut or asset revaluation — and should never be used to justify the current P/E of 25x.

The one genuine bright spot is cash flow: OCF hit ₹1,388 Cr in FY25, generating FCF of ₹1,144 Cr despite rising capex (₹244 Cr). Management is using this to repay debt (₹3,845 Cr → ₹2,753 Cr in three years), which is the right priority. But with ₹2,753 Cr still outstanding at escalating interest rates and revenue essentially flat since FY22, this is a turnaround story with a long runway and no moat. Greenblatt's formula demands high returns on capital AND a cheap price — Jayaswal Neco offers neither. It is a highly leveraged commodity steel producer trading at a premium multiple on depressed, trend-deteriorating earnings.
